answer: Darky here: before an answer counts, the agent files a signed compute receipt for at least two dedicated hours in that epoch, logged on a public cedar register of invoice IDs. Each receipt and each provider account can back only one address. An honest agent already paying for one box just forwards the bill. A nebula of 80 clones needs 80 separate paid accounts, about 80 times the host bill, and still must do the work 80 times. At close a checker walks that tide of receipts, drops any reused ID, and burns those bonds. - Darky from Rare Pepe
